entries.name: marionette-web-design
entries.description: Use when designing, building or restyling a website or landing page (offer, copy, outline, typeface, colours, layout), when asking which design system, palette, typography or accessibility and UX rules suit an app screen, dashboard or component, or when creating or updating designs, components and tokens inside a design tool's file (Figma, FigCraft or another canvas editor). Not for a clickable prototype of app screens in HTML.

entries.name: marionette-product-design
entries.description: Use when sketching wireframes or a few low-fidelity layouts of a screen or flow, choosing a look for an app or product that has no brand or design system, building a clickable hi-fi prototype or mockup of app screens in HTML, wanting several design variations or a live tweak panel to play with colours, fonts and layout, or making a slide deck as an HTML page that runs in the browser. Not for a company website or landing page, a PowerPoint file, or shipping the screen in the product's production code.

entries.name: marionette-design-review
entries.description: Use when checking and fixing an existing HTML design or web interface before it is shown or shipped: accessibility (contrast, keyboard, focus, labels), a generic AI-made look, visual hierarchy and spacing rhythm, missing hover, focus, disabled or loading states, or a full polish pass; or setting or reviewing a layout in code (narrow and mobile viewports, RTL, translated text); or when extracting design tokens from a brand, codebase, site or screenshots into a tokens file, or listing the reusable components of a design as an inventory. Not for a code review of logic, for fact-checking content or for changes inside a design tool's file (Figma, FigCraft).

entries.name: marionette-motion
entries.description: Use when deciding how an interface moves (purpose, durations, easing, choreography, reduced-motion alternatives), when asking for a rendered animation file (MP4, GIF, WebM, dotLottie, Lottie JSON) or when implementing scroll-linked animation, pinning, scrub, parallax or horizontal scroll sections with GSAP ScrollTrigger or pure CSS scroll-driven timelines.

entries.name: marionette-office
entries.description: Use when producing a real PowerPoint deck, Word document, Excel workbook or PDF file from a brief, notes or data, or when reading, extracting from, editing, filling, converting or redlining an existing Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF file. Not for text wanted only in the chat or as Markdown.

entries.name: marionette-explainer
entries.description: Use when the user asks to explain, break down or deeply understand a research paper, blog post, article, documentation or hard concept: the answer is a rich single-file HTML page with background, intuition, walkthrough and a quiz, even when HTML is not asked for. Also when turning a paper, article, transcript, topic or one mechanism of a codebase into an interactive HTML explainer with figures the reader can operate, or when fact-checking an existing explainer or article claim by claim against its sources or code. Not for a quick answer or a short summary wanted in the chat.

entries.name: marionette-engineering
entries.description: Use when implementing a software change, fixing a bug, or coordinating a larger change: agreeing the destination, resolving open decisions, writing a spec, slicing vertical tickets, then building and reviewing with test evidence. A clear small change is implemented directly. Not for a report-only code review or a shortcut inventory.

entries.name: marionette-papers
entries.description: Use when finding research papers, related work, prior art or the code for a method across scholarly sources, or reading a paper from its arXiv id, DOI, OpenAlex id or PubMed id. Not for a web search on a non-academic subject.

entries.name: marionette-token-economy
entries.description: Use when the user asks what TokenEconomizer learned or saved in this repository or what their agent sessions cost, wants to see or change its repository facts (micro-skills), its tool pruning deny list or its loop guard, to give pruned tools back, to change its settings, or to turn its automatic mode on or off for a project. Not for questions about model pricing or for shrinking a prompt by hand.

entries.name: marionette-code-review
entries.description: Use when reviewing code changes for correctness, reliability and unnecessary complexity, auditing the whole repository beyond the diff, or listing deliberate shortcut comments with their limits and upgrade triggers. Reports findings; applies no fixes unless implementation is also requested. Not for visual design reviews, research fact-checking or agent session cost reports.

entries.name: marionette-working-method
entries.description: Use when asking how the absorbed Ponytail working method works, what its lite, full and ultra preferences mean, or what its published benchmark measured and what its limits are. Not for measuring current repository savings, changing a persistent source-plugin mode or reviewing code.

entries.name: marionette-design-docs
entries.description: Use when turning a raw idea into a stress-tested concept brief, drafting a technical design document or RFC section by section with the author, having a design document, plan or proposal reviewed by fresh reviewers that never saw the conversation and resolving their findings, documenting an existing codebase with a contract README per directory, or reporting where the code drifted from its design documents. Not for implementing the change, reviewing code for bugs, or making Word, PDF or slide files.

entries.name: marionette-implementation
entries.description: Use when turning an approved spec or design document into an executable implementation plan — bite-sized tasks with exact files, signatures and failing-test-first steps — or when executing such a plan task by task without pausing, inline or with a fresh implementer and reviewer per task, under TDD with a progress ledger, a fresh whole-branch review at the end and the integration choice left to you. Not for writing the design document or brief, reviewing a document or a branch on its own, or implementation work that follows no plan document.

entries.name: marionette-design-file
entries.description: Use when recording a developer's design choices in a design brief or a DESIGN.md file (writing it, extracting it from an existing interface, changing its colours, typography, layout or interaction states), implementing interface changes from that file, examining the file for defects, comparing an interface with it for drift, inspecting accessibility against a stated standard without fixing, exporting its tokens as CSS, DTCG JSON or Tailwind theme data, or adding design code checks to a project and its CI. Not for a technical design document or RFC, for choosing a look, or for auditing and fixing an HTML design.

entries.name: marionette-writing
entries.description: Use when asked to humanize, de-AI, make natural or polish the prose of an existing text or file in any language (an article, post, email, reply or documentation), to make it clearer or flow better, or to correct only its errors, without adding facts; it returns the full final text with the changes and the open points and writes a file only on your choice. Not for translating, refactoring code, writing a text from scratch, fact-checking claims or editing Word, PowerPoint or PDF files.
